2.0.0.en: In those days: that is, the birth of John the Baptist.

2.0.1.en: Caesar Augustus: this is a title of the Roman emperor, whose name was Octavius.

2.0.2.en: All the world: the whole Roman kingdom, which included most of the world.

2.0.3.en: Syria: it includes the whole region of the Levant and Iraq, including Judea.

2.0.4.en: St. Luke takes care to determine the time of the birth of Christ. It was in the days of Caesar Augustus, emperor of the Roman state, when he issued a general census for his whole kingdom. This was the first census of his era, because he did this every ten years, and as a courtesy to the Jews he ordered that the census be taken by each one returning to his own homeland, because the Jews care about their lineage. This was by divine providence, to show that Jesus Christ is the son of David as the prophets foretold.

2.0.5.en: St. Luke also specifies the time of the general census, which was when Cyrenius was governor of Syria. The purpose of the census for the state was to collect tribute, but God's providence was to record the name of Jesus in history as a man and of the seed of David.

2.1.0.en: Went up: because Jerusalem and Bethlehem are higher in elevation than Galilee, in addition to the fact that one who goes to the capital is said to have gone up.

2.1.1.en: The Virgin Mary was living with her betrothed Joseph the carpenter in the city of Nazareth in Galilee, in the north of Judea near the Sea of Galilee. They had to register in Bethlehem, which is in the south of Judea near the Dead Sea and next to Jerusalem, a long distance of about 130 kilometers. How hard it was for the Virgin, pregnant in her ninth month and a girl of sixteen, and for the aged Joseph the carpenter, to make such an arduous journey, which took about four days.

2.2.0.en: In the city of Bethlehem, the city of David, in which the prophets foretold that Christ would be born (Mic 5:2), the Holy Family found no place to stay because of the great crowding, in addition to their poverty, which did not allow them to obtain reasonable shelter. The situation was made harder when the Virgin felt that her hour to give birth had come, so the family was forced to enter a cave where animals were kept. In this filthy stable the Virgin found no better place to lay her newborn than a small manger in which animals' food was put, after she had wrapped Him in some cloths.

2.2.1.en: Thus Christ found no place for Himself in the houses of men, so He was born in a place not for the dwelling of people but of animals, to break by His humility the pride of men.

2.2.2.en: And He was laid in the manger to be food not for animals but for the whole world, by His most holy Body and Blood. When St. Luke mentions her firstborn son, he means that He was her first child, and this does not mean that she had other children; rather the first child to be born is always called the firstborn, regardless of whether his mother will bear another after him or not. And of course the Virgin did not bear after Christ, since her womb was reserved for Christ alone, as Ezekiel the prophet mentions: "This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut" (Ezek 44:2).

2.2.3.en: Do you accept, my brother, to give up some of your comfort and needs in order to hold fast to God and to love others? Look at the humility of Christ and His endurance of people's refusal to receive Him, so that you will not grieve if people refuse to help you.

2.3.0.en: In the darkness of the night a great angel appeared with a strong light, and the simple shepherds were afraid; then the angel reassured them, and even declared that he was bringing good news for them and for all mankind.

2.4.0.en: The angel declared that the fullness of time had come, and that the awaited Messiah, the Savior of the world, was born. This is a clear declaration from heaven of the divinity of Christ, since he calls Him the Lord. The angel appeared to shepherds because they tend the sheep that were offered as sacrifices in the Temple to take away the sins of the people according to the Law of Moses, to announce to them the birth of Christ, the true Lamb to whom these sacrifices pointed, so that He might take away the sins of the whole world; for He is not merely a lord but the Lord, and none other.

2.5.0.en: The angel gave them a sign to confirm his good news and to make it easy to find Him: a child wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger in Bethlehem, that is, the city of David.

2.6.0.en: After this good news, heaven proclaimed its glorification of the holy Lord in the form of a multitude of angels who appeared with the angel, giving glory to God who was born in the manger, and who is also glorified by the heavenly ones, and who gives peace to man by taking his sins away from him; and then man worships God and his heart rejoices, after having angered Him in the Garden of Eden and being separated from Him for a long time, so that God is pleased with him and rejoices in him.

2.6.1.en: God is glorified in His angels, so keep vigil with the shepherds to praise Him in your prayers and share with the angels, and you will experience His work in your heart and rejoice in Him.

2.6.2.en: Enjoy the praises from the Book of the Midnight Praise along with the prayers of the Agpeya every day.

2.7.s.en: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

2.7.0.en: The shepherds' joy at the angels' good news was great, so they hastened to Bethlehem, near which they had been keeping watch, searching all the stables and caves for the great Child.

2.8.0.en: How great was the shepherds' joy when they found the Child in the manger with His mother the Virgin Mary and the aged Joseph, and they told Joseph and Mary of the angel's good news to them about the birth of Christ the Savior.

2.9.0.en: Because of the shepherds' abundant exultation, a number of Jews, with whom Bethlehem was crowded because of the census, gathered and heard the shepherds' good news, but they could not grasp the mystery of the Incarnation although they witnessed it, and were content with wonder and astonishment.

2.10.0.en: The Virgin kept the shepherds' good news with faith and spiritual understanding, pondering its meanings, which confirm the divinity of Christ. This means that St. Luke drew his Gospel from the Virgin Mary, who told him what she felt in her heart.

2.10.1.en: This also shows the Virgin's distinction from the people of Bethlehem, who were content with wonder, and also from the shepherds, who praised God, for she meditated deeply, and her faith in the divinity of Christ was confirmed.

2.10.2.en: Do you meditate on the words of the Holy Bible and apply them in your life every day as the voice of God to you? And do you see God in the events around you and in people's words, so that everything leads you to repentance and the knowledge of God?

2.11.0.en: The shepherds returned to the place of their folds outside Bethlehem, but with hearts changed from material preoccupation to praising God because of what they had heard from the angel and what they had seen inside the cattle stable, namely Christ who was born.

2.12.s.en: (4) The circumcision of Christ and the purification of the Virgin

2.12.0.en: Since Christ condescended by His Incarnation, He also humbled Himself in submitting to the Law, though He had no need of it, but He fulfilled all righteousness on our behalf. So He was circumcised on the eighth day as God commanded Abraham, as a sign for him and for all his descendants in their bodies, declaring their allegiance to God and their distinction from unbelievers.

2.12.1.en: Circumcision is a type of Baptism, in which there is a cutting off of the evil nature and the beginning of a new life with God; and circumcision is called in our colloquial speech "purification of males."

2.12.2.en: It was the Jewish custom to name the child on this day, so He was named Jesus, that is, Savior, as the angel Gabriel declared in his good news to the Virgin Mary.

2.13.0.en: The Law of Moses decreed (Lev 12:5, 1) that the woman who has given birth should not enter the Temple for forty days in the case of a male child, or eighty days in the case of a female child, and she was considered unclean during this period. In the New Testament the Church has also kept this period, considering it a period of bodily rest and spiritual repentance ... but of what is she to repent?!?

2.13.1.en: The woman must not forget, amid the joys of her giving birth, that she has borne a child who carries the sin of Adam and Eve, in which the woman was a direct cause.

2.13.2.en: And her period of repentance ends with her newborn child's attaining salvation in the holy sacrament of Baptism, and then she presents herself with him for the communion of the divine Mysteries.

2.14.0.en: Openeth the womb: that is, firstborn.

2.14.1.en: Holy: sanctified and consecrated to God.

2.14.2.en: The firstborn was presented for the service of the Lord, or was redeemed by presenting a sum to the Temple, because when God killed the firstborn of the Egyptians He said to His people that their firstborn, whom He had redeemed by the slaying of the Passover lamb on their behalf, had become His own (Ex 13:2, 12). The tribe of Levi was consecrated to Him, but as for the firstborn of the rest of the people, each one gave a ransom for himself, a sum of money, to the Temple.

2.15.0.en: For her purification the mother offered a lamb and a young pigeon, the first as a burnt offering and the second as a sin offering, a reference to Christ who by His Cross and death pleased God as a burnt offering and took away our iniquities ... but in the case of the poor, like the Virgin and Joseph, they offered a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons. The pigeon is a symbol of simplicity, and the turtledove of the beautiful voice, that is, the preaching of the word of God.

2.15.1.en: Christ emptied Himself and fulfilled the Law in order to be like us in everything. May you share the lives of those around you, so that you feel for them and show your love for them, even with few words that draw them to you, and they open their hearts to you and find rest from many troubles.

2.16.s.en: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

2.16.0.en: Near the Temple in Jerusalem there lived an old man named Simeon, distinguished by righteousness and goodness in his relationship with those around him and by devoutness in his worship of God, waiting for the Messiah of whom the prophecies of the prophets in Israel had spoken, to give salvation and consolation to his people. The Holy Spirit was upon him, for in the Old Testament He came upon some people for specified periods, which differs from His permanent dwelling in the New Testament inside the believers. Church tradition tells us that this Simeon was among the seventy-two elders whom King Ptolemy in Egypt chose to translate the Torah into Greek, and he doubted the words of Isaiah about the conception of the Virgin, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (Isa 7:14), and wanted to translate it "a young woman," but God declared to him that he should translate it as it is, that is, "virgin," and even promised him that he would see with his own eyes the fulfillment of this verse.

2.17.0.en: One day the Holy Spirit moved Simeon the elder to go to the Temple, where a great number of fathers and mothers had gathered with their children, and large numbers of the people had come to offer sacrifices and to give a ransom for their firstborn children. The Holy Spirit guided him to the Child Jesus as He was entering the Temple with His mother for them to pay the ransom for Him according to the custom of the Jews, as we mentioned. So Simeon took Him and carried Him in his arms and raised his voice in praise and blessing to God, who was carried by him and who is in the highest.

2.18.0.en: According to thy word: because God had promised him that he would live until he saw the Virgin bear the awaited Messiah, so he lived longer than the usual span of men until he saw Christ, and he longed to depart to heaven.

2.18.1.en: Thy salvation: that is, Christ the Savior.

2.18.2.en: All people: because Christ is the Savior of the whole world, Jews and Gentiles.

2.18.3.en: Simeon declared in his song of praise that he had witnessed the fulfillment of the prophecy of Isaiah, for he saw Christ the Lord, the Savior of the whole world, not only as consolation and glory for Israel but as a light for the whole world, bringing them back from idolatry to faith in the true God, and saving all from their sins. And since he enjoyed the sight of God, he was satisfied and rejoiced, and no longer needed to live in this world but to depart to eternity, confident in the redemption of Christ. Because of the importance of this song of praise, the Church repeats it in the prayer of sleep in the Agpeya every day, and in the midnight prayer, and also in the Midnight Praise.

2.18.4.en: Come, my brother, to the Temple today to behold salvation in the Body and Blood of the Lord on the altar, as salvation for you from all your sins and as strength and light for your life, so that you are filled with vitality and satisfaction and your eyes are lifted up to the constant union with God in eternity; and to the extent that you enjoy Holy Communion you behold God, and you fear nothing, not even death.

2.19.0.en: Joseph the carpenter and the Virgin Mary marveled at God's declaring the good news of salvation to Simeon the elder, as the angel Gabriel had earlier announced to them the good news of the Nativity, and they were also astonished that this salvation is not limited to the Jews but is likewise for the Gentiles.

2.19.1.en: It is made clear here that the Virgin is the mother of Christ, and Joseph is not His father, though it appears so before people, and this is mentioned in (v. 27), that they are His parents as people suppose.

2.20.0.en: Simeon, who was filled with the Holy Spirit, also blessed Joseph and Mary, and declared to the Virgin, who would see with her own eyes the preaching of Christ (for Joseph would die before this), how some would believe and be saved and rise from their sins, while many would refuse to believe and be condemned, and how the sign of Christ would be spoken against, which is the Cross on which the redemption of the world would be accomplished.

2.21.0.en: A sword: the meaning is figurative, that is, severe sufferings.

2.21.1.en: Thoughts may be revealed: the evils of those who opposed Christ and crucified Him will appear.

2.21.2.en: Simeon also declared to the Virgin that she would suffer many pains when she would see the Jews' opposition to her Son, and would even see His sufferings and crucifixion, as the ninth hour prayer in the Agpeya recalls, and when she would see the thoughts and evils of the scribes, the Pharisees and the priests of the Jews who crucified Christ, who even opposed the Virgin until the end of her life.

2.22.s.en: (6) The song of praise of Anna the daughter of Phanuel

2.22.0.en: St. Luke continues to tell us about God's announcements of the birth of the Messiah to those who were waiting for it and were concerned with His birth, for God reveals Himself to those who seek Him. And in the company of the elders Anna joins Simeon, for God announced the good news of His birth to the elders in appreciation of their wisdom and perseverance in spiritual striving with Him.

2.22.1.en: Anna means "God's grace," Phanuel "the face of God," and Aser "rich." Her name has a beautiful meaning that gives hope amid afflictions, since her life appears hard because of her husband's death after seven years of marriage; she was a young woman, probably no more than twenty-five years old, but she was able to fill her emptiness with the love of God. She lived near the Temple, occupied with prayers and worship, and in asceticism she even fasted much to free herself from everything and deepen her relationship with God. She lived 84 years in this life, and probably her earlier life was bound to God in preparation for a deeper relationship with Him.

2.22.2.en: She is a great picture of perseverance, an example for all widows and a hope for those who suffer from emptiness or afflictions. She had passed a hundred years and was still in much worship, waiting for Christ the Savior. Does affliction drive you to cling to God? And do you try to fill your emptiness with prayers, readings and service? Do you persevere in your striving even if God's answer to your prayers is delayed for many long years?

2.23.0.en: The Holy Spirit, who came upon her, led her to meet the Virgin and Joseph and to enjoy seeing the Child Jesus carried in Simeon's arms. She began to praise God and to speak prophecies about the redemption and salvation that this Child would accomplish. Many of those who offered worship in the Temple, waiting for the Messiah the Savior, gathered, and heard Anna's words and praise, and enjoyed seeing the Child Jesus Christ.

2.24.0.en: After they had completed what the Law commanded in Jerusalem, St. Luke mentions that they returned to Nazareth, but this did not happen quickly, as is understood from (Mt 2); it took several years, for they lived a period in Bethlehem where the Magi visited them, then came Herod's order to kill the children, so they fled to Egypt and stayed there for a time, then returned to Nazareth, passing through Judea.

2.25.0.en: St. Luke comments on the life of Christ from His early childhood to the age of twelve, which He lived in Nazareth, that He grew in His childhood like an ordinary human being. How wonderful it is that God emptied Himself to become man and grow like the rest of mankind, although in His divinity He is perfect from eternity.

2.25.1.en: We have no information about this period, but it is understood from the context of the verses that Joseph and Mary were concerned about the worship of God, and about visiting Jerusalem and offering sacrifices every year, so they brought Him up in a religious upbringing and taught Him the Holy Scriptures in the synagogue. But He was distinguished by His submission to the Holy Spirit in Him, so His growth, strength, spirituality and wisdom appeared, and grace overflowed upon Him as a perfect man, an example for all of us.

2.25.2.en: To the extent that you submit to God and the Church and are bound to her, God's grace and wisdom overflow upon you.

2.26.s.en: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

2.26.0.en: The Gospel shows here Joseph and Mary's adherence to the worship of God, and their going to Jerusalem yearly at the official feasts, the most important of which was the feast of the Passover, which they first kept in Egypt and after which they went out into the wilderness. It is a clear type of the redemption of Christ on the Cross and of partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

2.27.0.en: After the custom of the feast: that is, they completed the rites of the feast of the Passover.

2.27.1.en: When Jesus reached the age of twelve, which is the age at which a person is bound to complete all the religious rites according to the law of the Jews, since it is the age of discernment after the stage of childhood in which discernment is partial, He went with Joseph and Mary, as was their custom at the feast of the Passover, to Jerusalem.

2.27.2.en: During the feast a great number of teachers would gather in circles inside the Temple, and around them the Jews would ask them about various fields of worship and the spiritual life.

2.27.3.en: After completing the rites of the feast, they departed, returning to their city Nazareth, and the custom was to travel in caravans for fear of robbers. The caravan was divided into two parts: in front the women with the small children, and the second part the men, while the youths, of whose age Jesus was, would walk at the front or the rear. Jesus lingered in the Temple among the teachers, asking them, conversing with them and answering them, and Joseph and Mary did not know this.

2.28.0.en: After a day's journey from Jerusalem to the north on the road to Nazareth, that is, about twenty miles, they had to spend the night and rest, so Joseph asked Mary about her son Jesus and did not find Him with her, and she also discovered that He was not with Joseph. They began to look for Him among the relatives and acquaintances in the caravan, but unfortunately did not find Him, so they returned another day's journey to Jerusalem and kept searching for Him everywhere.

2.28.1.en: They suffered greatly because of Joseph's old age and the physical strain on them. They did not suspect that an accident might have befallen Him, because of the angel's good news and the many heavenly announcements, but perhaps they thought that He had lost the way and wandered far away somewhere, or that He had ascended to heaven and deprived them of seeing Him for a time, and this tormented them greatly. At last, at the end of the third day, they found Jesus in the Temple, sitting among the teachers.

2.29.0.en: The Virgin, with Joseph, noticed Jesus' distinction and His superiority over the teachers in His questions and answers, and all who heard Him were amazed and marveled with them.

2.30.0.en: How great was the joy of the Virgin and Joseph when they found Him! The Virgin expressed the extent of the suffering she had endured with Joseph in feeling His loss, and the Virgin's humility appears in her putting Joseph before herself when she said, "Thy father and I"; here it means his responsibility for Him as a father, although He was not of his seed, as the Gospels make clear.

2.31.0.en: Jesus alerted His mother and Joseph to the heavenly announcements they had heard about Him and His work as Savior, and His eternal sonship to God, and that He must accomplish His purpose, that is, the aim for which the Father sent Him into the world.

2.32.0.en: These words were hard for her to understand, but the Virgin realized the importance of these words and kept them in her heart until God would interpret them to her later.

2.32.1.en: Jesus' concern for His sonship to God and His accomplishing His purposes does not mean His neglecting His sonship to His mother; rather He submitted in obedience to her and to Joseph to give us a wonderful example in obeying parents. The Virgin also gives us an example of true motherhood in breadth of heart and leaving children to live according to their gifts and abilities, and not according to a fixed picture of what fathers and mothers want.

2.32.2.en: Honor your elders, especially your parents, and submit to them and offer your love to all, and do not force anyone to behave as you want, and give freedom to everyone, and to your children, as long as their behavior is not evil.

2.33.0.en: Here is the last mention of Joseph the carpenter, and he probably died in the following years, about which we have no details except this verse, from the age of 12 to 30, for he is not referred to at the beginning of Christ's preaching ministry, but only the Virgin. This means that Christ began to work as a carpenter and bore responsibility for His mother after Joseph.

2.33.1.en: Luke speaks about His life as a man, how He continued to grow in all aspects, psychological, bodily and spiritual, and this was evident before people, but rather before God.

2.33.2.en: The announcement of the Baptist and the Baptism of Christ
